svg.aria-label: Picking keys without scoring all of them. Left, naive top-k: a query scores all N keys, keeps the top k and takes a softmax over those, but it has already paid for all N scores, so it is still quadratic. Right, three cheaper ways to find candidates. (a) Hash or cluster the keys into buckets, with LSH or k-means centroids, and the query only scores the keys inside its own bucket. (b) Native Sparse Attention, NSA, 2025: three branches per query, a compressed branch where each block of keys is squashed into one coarse token, a selected branch that reads the top-scoring blocks by those coarse scores at full resolution, and a sliding window over the most recent tokens, mixed by a learned gate. (c) DeepSeek Sparse Attention, DSA, 2025: a tiny indexer with few heads in FP8 scores every past position and hands the top-k to the real attention, so it still touches every position but is far cheaper than full attention.
svg.text: a learned gate mixes the three
but far cheaper than full attention
